papers.title: Corrosion-fatigue of L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V lattice struts: role of geometrical imperfections under simulated physiological conditions
papers.abstract: • Corrosion–fatigue of L-PBF Ti-6Al-4 V lattice struts studied at 60° build orientation. • Fatigue life governed by extreme surface valleys • PBS environment reduces high-cycle fatigue strength by ∼ 25% at 10⁶ cycles. • XCT identifies surface-connected valleys as dominant crack initiation sites. • Environment-assisted crack propagation confirmed by fractography and EDXS. The corrosion-fatigue behaviour of laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) Ti-6Al-4 V lattice struts was investigated with particular emphasis on the role of manufacturing-induced geometrical imperfections. Thin strut specimens representing strut-based lattice sub-unit elements were built at a 60° orientation and tested under tension–tension loading (R = 0.1) in laboratory air and in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) at 37 °C. Micro-computed tomography was employed to quantify surface roughness, geometrical deviations, and the interaction between surface valleys and near-surface porosity. Quasi-static tensile tests showed limited scatter in strength and ductility, indicating that monotonic behaviour is governed by global geometry. In contrast, fatigue performance was strongly defect-sensitive. While comparable fatigue strength was observed in air and PBS in the low-cycle regime, exposure to PBS led to a marked reduction in high-cycle fatigue strength, reaching approximately 25% at 10⁶ cycles. Fractographic and EDXS analyses revealed that fatigue cracks initiated at surface-connected valleys in both environments, whereas the physiological environment primarily accelerated crack propagation through corrosion-assisted mechanisms and suppressed crack branching. A micro-CT-based deepest-valley analysis showed good agreement between predicted critical defects and experimental failure locations. The results highlight the dominant role of extreme surface geometrical imperfections and environment-assisted crack growth in the fatigue behaviour of L-PBF Ti-6Al-4 V lattice structures.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文直接研究增材制造Ti-6Al-4V点阵支柱的腐蚀疲劳行为，包含实验验证，完全符合L1方向对力学和疲劳性能的要求。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not cover as-built mechanical properties of bulk Ti-6Al-4V; it focuses on lattice struts and corrosion-fatigue, but it is still within L1 scope.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究制造缺陷和生理环境对L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V点阵支柱腐蚀疲劳行为的影响。
summary_zh.method: 对60°构建方向的薄支柱试样进行空气和PBS环境下的拉-拉疲劳实验，结合micro-CT表征。
summary_zh.result: PBS环境下高周疲劳强度降低约25%，表面山谷缺陷主导裂纹萌生。
summary_zh.validation: 通过断口分析和EDXS验证环境辅助裂纹扩展机制。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the combined effects of manufacturing-induced geometrical imperfections and a physiological environment on the corrosion-fatigue behavior of L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V lattice struts.
summary_en.method: Thin strut specimens built at 60° orientation were tested under tension-tension fatigue in air and PBS at 37°C, with micro-CT characterization of surface roughness and porosity.
summary_en.result: Fatigue life was defect-sensitive; PBS reduced high-cycle fatigue strength by about 25% at 10^6 cycles, with surface valleys dominating crack initiation.
summary_en.validation: Fractography and EDXS confirmed environment-assisted crack propagation, and micro-CT deepest-valley analysis predicted critical defects consistent with failure locations.
